chunks: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) struck a slave, then he entered his house, brought out a whip, then stripped himself of his shirt for the slave, then said to him: 'Strike 'Ali ibn al-Husayn [for having struck you]!' but the servant refused, so he gave him fifty dinars.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin do after striking his slave?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, highlights the concept of *adl* (justice) and *tawadu* (humility) within the Ahl al-Bayt, where the Imam voluntarily subjected himself to the same penalty he imposed on his slave. The narrative underscores the spiritual merit of freeing slaves or compensating them as an act of expiation (*kaffarah*) for minor disciplinary actions, reflecting the refined etiquette of the Imams. It serves as a practical model for masters in Shia jurisprudence regarding the equitable treatment and moral elevation of slaves.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī said, “I heard Abā al-Ḥasan (a) say, ‘ʿAlī ibn al- Ḥusayn (a) struck a slave [of his], then he entered his house and came out with a whip. He then took off his shirt and said to him, ‘Whip ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn [for his having struck you]!’ but the servant refused, so he gave him fifty dīnārs.”[1]
